subject: forensic-medicine
title: Carbon Monoxide: Carboxyhaemoglobin, Cherry Red Blood and CO Automatism

steps.title: Carbon monoxide, the silent chemical asphyxiant
steps.tx: **Carbon monoxide** is a colourless, tasteless, non irritative gas from incomplete combustion of carbon, insoluble in water, burning with a blue flame and lighter than air, gathering at one and a half to two metres in closed rooms and seeping through cracks and plasterboard through whole houses. It binds haemoglobin with two hundred to three hundred times oxygen's affinity into stable carboxyhaemoglobin, and forty times affinity for myoglobin, while also blocking cytochrome oxidase and shifting the dissociation curve left so tissues starve beyond the anaemia.
steps.say: Two hundred times oxygen's grip on haemoglobin and a left shifted curve make CO a chemical asphyxiant that hides in plain air.

steps.title: Saturation bands and symptoms
steps.tx: **Carboxyhaemoglobin percentage predicts the picture**. Zero to ten percent: no appreciable symptoms. Ten to twenty: breathlessness on moderate exertion, mild headache and weakness. Twenty to thirty: throbbing headache, irritability, emotional instability, disturbed judgement, defective memory and rapid fatigue. Thirty to forty: severe headache, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, dim vision and confusion. Forty to fifty: confusion, hallucinations, severe ataxia, rapid breathing and collapse resembling alcoholic intoxication, with cherry red colour appearing.
steps.say: Headache at ten, throbbing confusion at thirty and drunken collapse at fifty: saturation writes the symptoms in advance.

steps.title: Coma, death and lowered lethal levels
steps.tx: At fifty to sixty percent come syncope or coma with intermittent convulsions, rapid respirations, tachycardia with weak pulse and pink red skin; sixty to seventy deepens coma with incontinence; seventy to eighty brings profound coma, absent reflexes, thready pulse and shallow irregular breathing to death; above eighty, rapid respiratory arrest. Death usually needs **eighty percent saturation**, but senility, heart or lung disease, anaemia, hypnotics and alcohol can kill from as little as thirty percent.
steps.say: Eighty percent kills the healthy, thirty percent can kill the old, anaemic or drunk, so comorbidity rewrites the lethal level.

steps.title: Cherry red blood and postmortem staining
steps.tx: **Cherry red discolouration** of skin, blood and postmortem staining is carbon monoxide's autopsy signature, because cells cannot extract oxygen from carboxyhaemoglobin and the blood stays bright under the skin instead of turning blue. Platelet aggregation is inhibited. Bullae from skin hypoxia appear at calves, buttocks, wrists and knees, separate and isolated with thick cellular fluid and surrounding inflammation, mistakable for second degree burns but rarely touching fingers and toes. CO is not absorbed by a body after death, separating antemortem exposure cleanly.
steps.say: Cherry red lividity, bright blood and pressure bullae mark CO death, and a corpse in CO air absorbs none of it.

steps.title: CO automatism: the disturbed room
steps.tx: The dying CO victim may make **wild erratic swinging movements** inside the room, disturbing clothing and furniture and giving an impression of violent struggle, called CO automatism. More than one death investigation has chased a murderer through a room wrecked by its own victim. The scene discipline follows: photograph before touching, measure carboxyhaemoglobin in every body found, and test the appliance and air before reconstructing any assault from disorder alone.
steps.say: A wrecked room with a cherry red body may be the victim's own automatism, not a struggle with any murderer.

steps.title: Sources: heaters, engines and cigarettes
steps.tx: **CO sources** are coal gas, fire smoke and defective furnaces, stoves, water heaters, fireplaces and oil lamps, a yellow flame generating CO while a blue flame burns clean. Mine explosions leave after damp, badly ventilated collieries choke damp, and motor exhaust holds one to seven percent CO, poisoning a small garage in five to ten minutes, diesel far less than petrol. Industry makes about twenty percent of cases. A pack a day smoker runs five to six percent saturation, heavy smokers fifteen to twenty, traffic policemen up to ten.
steps.say: Yellow flames, garage exhaust in ten minutes and even cigarettes at six percent saturate blood from everyday sources.

right.title: Background saturation
points: Pack a day smoker, 5 to 6 percent

steps.title: Elimination and oxygen therapy
steps.tx: **CO elimination** is through the lungs alone, about one percent metabolised to carbon dioxide, none through skin, bile, sweat, urine or faeces. Half life is four to five hours breathing room air, eighty to ninety minutes on one hundred percent oxygen, and under thirty minutes under hyperbaric oxygen at three atmospheres. Treatment is therefore removal and oxygen at the highest available concentration, with hyperbaric referral for coma, pregnancy and cardiac involvement in modern practice.
steps.say: Four hours on air, ninety minutes on pure oxygen and thirty under pressure: oxygen is the whole antidote strategy.

steps.title: Fetal poisoning and delayed brain injury
steps.tx: CO crosses to the fetus, where **fetal carboxyhaemoglobin runs ten to fifteen percent higher than maternal**, so intrauterine death can occur though the mother survives. Survivors of CO poisoning may develop neurological sequelae within two to four weeks: tremors, personality change, memory impairment, monoplegia, hemiplegia, psychosis, peripheral neuropathy, visual loss, poor concentration and Parkinsonism. Children saturate faster than adults for their higher respiratory exchange, and physical activity during exposure accelerates saturation.
steps.say: The fetus saturates above its mother and may die while she lives, and survivors can declare Parkinsonism a month later.

steps.title: CO in fire deaths ties back to burns
steps.tx: In burnt bodies, **carboxyhaemoglobin proves breathing during the fire** alongside soot in the terminal bronchioles, the pair built in the thermal module. Heat haematoma blood carries the same CO saturation as peripheral blood, separating it from a pre fire extradural bleed. A body burnt after death shows neither deep soot nor raised saturation. Every charred body therefore gets blood CO estimation with the soot examination, before putrefaction destroys both witnesses.
steps.say: Soot below the cords plus raised CO convict the fire of killing a living breather; neither appears in a body burnt dead.
